clue.text: People move quickly south of a European meeting place

indicators.note: in a down entry, being south of something means sitting below it, so these pieces follow the earlier ones

parts.note: a Scot is a European from Scotland
a race is a people or ethnic group
to course is to run or flow fast

explanation.surface: Crowds hurry past a continental venue where people gather.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot. 'south of' places RACE COURSE below A SCOT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A race meeting is held at a racecourse, so a racecourse is a venue for that kind of gathering.

clue.text: Fast and loose, by the sound of it?

definitions.meaning: ... as in 'a ... pace', meaning brisk or quick

definitions.text: loose, by the sound of it?
definitions.meaning: something loose shakes and clatters, so you can hear it is loose

explanation.surface: A wry comment on something both speedy and wobbly, judged by its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk pace is called rattling, and a loose part makes a clattering noise as it shakes.

clue.text: Toy bags in supermarket, very clear

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or enclose, so the toy word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
taken as written
ASDA is a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Someone notices a toy dropped into shopping bags at a supermarket, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like shopping bags but is the insertion signal: PLAY holds IN and ASDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something utterly obvious, as evident as daylight.

clue.text: Level of interest bishop's shown over a frightful teaser

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so the bishop's letter comes first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: frightful suggests something mangled and messy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric's concern is aroused by a dreadful brain-teaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level of interest' sounds like curiosity but means a bank's lending rate; 'shown over' puts the bishop on top in the down entry, and 'frightful' shuffles the teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A central bank's headline rate sets the general cost of borrowing for lenders and savers.

clue.text: Bird, parrot's first sweetheart

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the parrot word

parts.note: a sweetheart is a lover

explanation.surface: A pet parrot's earliest beloved, given as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover is a wading shore bird, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Place power in bullet — that should get things motoring!

indicators.note: the place and power pieces sit inside the bullet word

parts.note: a slug is a bullet
to park something is to place or put it
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Instructions to load energy into a bullet, promising it will get things moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A car engine's ignition depends on this part's spark firing the fuel, so it gets the motor running.

clue.text: Cinema of a sort not showing Rambo originally, go for it!

indicators.note: not showing means the letter is left out, punning on what a cinema screens

parts.note: a drive-in is an outdoor cinema watched from cars

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of the action hero's name

explanation.surface: A film fan is urged on, at a cinema that isn't screening Rambo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not showing' drops R, the first of Rambo, from DRIVE-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges someone to start eagerly, like plunging into water, so it means go ahead and begin.

clue.text: Voice in my ear came in preposterous Trump mission?

indicators.note: the voice word goes inside the jumbled letters
preposterous means absurd, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: bass is a singing voice, the lowest

explanation.surface: Someone hears a ridiculous voice in their ear about a Trump errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preposterous' scrambles MY EAR CAME IN to AMERICANEMY, and BASS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission, and one run by the United States would be the mission of a Trump government.

clue.text: Post-hermaphrodite gender reported?

parts.note: a snail is a hermaphrodite, having both sexes

indicators.note: reported means heard, so the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: male is one gender

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which gender follows hermaphroditism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post-hermaphrodite' reads as one word but splits: Post is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent through the ordinary postal service, slow compared with email, are jokingly called this.

clue.text: Mythological king, one being carried like a baby?

indicators.note: being carried means held inside, so the letter goes in the baby carriage word

parts.note: a baby is carried in a pram
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A legendary monarch, carried about as if he were an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend during the Trojan War.

clue.text: Bare bones revealed rank

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a rank is a line, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: A skeleton exposed, laid out in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch giving only the main points, without detail, is the bare bones of a plan.

clue.text: Painter gives extremely detailed subject of self-portrait to sovereign

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: extremely means very
in a self-portrait the subject is me
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An artist presents a meticulous self-portrait to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'precise' but means de-tailed: VERY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch Golden Age artist, known for Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: Resurgent Australian openers batting — what might stop them?

indicators.note: openers, besides cricket batsmen, are the first letters of these words

parts.note: a cricketer who is batting is in

explanation.surface: Australia's opening batsmen are back in form at the crease, and only weather could halt them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' reads as cricket's opening batsmen but takes first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather halts a cricket match, so a shower could stop batsmen in their tracks.

clue.text: Australian native with overwhelming fear of beard, perhaps?

parts.note: a beard is an example of something hairy
panic is sudden overwhelming fear

explanation.surface: An Australian has a terror of facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests a person; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grass that grows wild in Australia, so it is a native species there.

clue.text: General appearance supermarket admits indefensible, initially

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: garb is clothing, one's outward appearance

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A general look of a supermarket that confesses to being indefensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the Italian military commander who led the fight for unification.

clue.text: Allied force at once circling German capital

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the capital
to force is to wrench out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
a capital is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Allied army immediately surrounds Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' shuffles AT ONCE, which then goes round G, the capital of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related or akin, as words sharing a root are, so it means connected.

clue.text: Drop a scam for starters?

indicators.note: for here means on behalf of, putting the course word beside the scam word

parts.note: soup is a typical starter
a con is a scam

explanation.surface: An invitation to abandon a fraud just for beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb but is a noun: a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a very small amount, a trace, like a drop of liquid.

clue.text: Get down in type of dance — evidently hot?

indicators.note: the eating word sits inside the dance word

parts.note: swing is a style of dance
to get food down is to eat it

explanation.surface: Getting down to some swing dancing, visibly overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' suggests dancing; it means swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration shows that someone is overheated, so it is visible proof of heat.

clue.text: Scholar wild about English hymn tunes

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the English letter
wild suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic gets furious over English church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately Lutheran hymn melody, so the plural means sacred tunes.

clue.text: Clubs with a three iron shortly exchanged for old driver

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped about, so these letters are rearranged
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A golfer swaps clubs for a three iron, playing the old driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' and 'clubs' suggest golf. 'shortly' trims IRON to IRO; 'exchanged' shuffles A THREE IRO into HARIOTEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a chariot in ancient times, so a driver of the old kind.

clue.text: See 22
In tip, taste cans

indicators.note: to can something is to enclose it, so the taste word holds the tip word

parts.note: to try food is to taste it
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A cryptic order to taste something in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: What is in is fashionable and in vogue.

clue.text: Previous character in audition, await your turn

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: former means previous; Q is a character, a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A past actor at an audition waits to be called.
explanation.walkthrough: FORMER Q spoken sounds like the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining up is how one waits in turn, so the phrase means wait for your go.

clue.text: See 3
Knocked over, Greek character and singer howl

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Lulu is a Scottish pop singer

explanation.surface: A Greek and a singer are bowled over and wail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ululating is a long wailing cry, so it is a form of howling.

clue.text: Good man fed to unpleasant chap a Mexican dish

indicators.note: fed to means put into, so the saint goes inside

parts.note: a toad is a contemptible person
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A saint is served to a nasty fellow, along with Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a crisp fried tortilla with toppings, a Mexican dish.

clue.text: £6 (not 9) for seafood

indicators.note: not means without, so the numeral is removed

parts.note: six pounds is six quid in British slang
IX is the Roman numeral nine

explanation.surface: A price tag of six pounds, not nine, for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid, eaten as calamari, is a kind of seafood.

clue.text: A prophet appearing reflective after dropping trousers

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces behind the dropping word

parts.note: dung is animal droppings

indicators.note: reflective means mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A prophet looks thoughtful after his trousers fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are work trousers with a bib and straps.
